Dear Jacob

This is a general R question you are asking: tsDyn is a R package, which you need to load (after having installed) with library(tsDyn), all the functions like TVECM  will be directly available (with their hidden internal dependencies), and you won't have to care for anything else.

Best

Matthieu

messages.subject: Re: [tsDyn] Re: Dear. tsdyn developers and users
parts:
Hi

Oh nice if you do a replication, I'll be happy to see the results (eventually putting them online as demo of tsDyn) if you don't mind?

the best value for the grid search is the highest value you can (but not bigger than n*(1-2*trim) for th) have.

Note indeed that there are arguments th1, th2 to specify the grid search, and you can always plug-in specified values. So you can estimate with a large grid,  restrict the grid to a smaller area, plug-in the value from the authors, and compare for each of these model the SSR (function deviance () ) you obtained

You can also specify the beta value with beta, so could try the 1,-1

Yo can also exclude constants in the VECM. On the other side, the ECT is computed without constant in any case.

Hope this helps

Matthieu

thanks for your help. it really works well after following what you said.  ^________________________^

in fact, i have a couple of questions regarding TVECM options such as ngridth/ngridG(number of elements to search for the threshold values)

 i am trying to replicate a TVECM-result from TVECM-related dissertation-"price dynamics under the presence of threshold effects in WTI crude oil markets by Eun-Young Kim"

i collected  the 936 observations(for regime1). they are exactly same as the observations in the dissertation in terms of mean and so on. 

but when i analyse the obs with TVECM(tsdyn R code), its outcome is not same as the one in the dissertation.

the dissertation says that the threshold value: -0.00073, 0.007736 but the value i got from my running TVECM is below: 

Best threshold from first search -0.02611572
Best cointegrating value 0.9970493
Second best (conditionnal on the first one) -0.02611572 0.00700082       SSR 1.422707
Second step best thresholds -0.0289955 0.00700082        


i found whenever i change the value for ngridth/ngridG  option, the outcome for the threshold value is slightly different.
so here is my question: .....is there any way to determine the best value for  ngridth/ngridG??


and another issues, according to the dissertation, it mentions some of options it used such as 
1) did not include constant term and time trend term in this model  
2) the error correction term without constant term and a co-integration vector of (1,-1)' to equate error correction term with basis 
3) and they used nthresh=2 and lag=2 

below is what i did for the above condition. 

tv<-TVECM(data_ln,lag=2, bn=100, ngridG=50, trim=0.01, nthresh=2,plot=TRUE, 
dummyToBothRegimes=TRUE, methodMapply=FALSE, 
gamma1=list(exact=NULL, int=c("from","to"), around="val"),
gamma2=list(exact=NULL, int=c("from","to"), around="val"), 
beta=list(exact=NULL, int=c("from","to"), around=c("val","by")),                       <- the calculated beta values are 1 and -0.9987. they are close to 1 and -1. so i let them default 
restr="none", 
model=c("All", "only_ECT"), include ="none",beta0=0,trace=TRUE )  


is there something wrong with my options???
